targets.wps-bad:
Documented position. France welcomes Germany's resolution 2467 as a milestone, not the end of the struggle against conflict-related sexual violence. It values the strengthened mandate of Special Representative Pramila Patten, survivor-centred approach and requested Secretary-General report by 2021 on children born of rape. It deplores concessions under permanent-member veto pressure, including removed health language and threats to 25 years of women's rights. Denying sexual/reproductive care to victims of atrocities undermines dignity. France defends comprehensive care and rights in every context, including women's free bodily decisions and the choice to terminate involuntary pregnancies. It will continue promoting this in the Council, other UN bodies and elsewhere. Reaffirmed WPS resolutions remain the framework, including 2106 paragraph 19 and 1889 paragraph 10; 2467's omission does not erase them. France renews the fight against conflict-related sexual violence.

Analytical application. X omits care/choice and makes criminal conviction an access gate; revise both. Release consent-based services immediately, including pregnancy-choice support; pursue confidential voluntary evidence and accountability in parallel. Independent care may provide fewer immediate investigative leads, a cost to manage without compelled reporting or delayed treatment. Historical health omissions remain criticisms of 2467, not acceptance of X.

Authority. Welcoming 2467 does not endorse X or guarantee a future vote; the real ongoing care commitment remains.

targets.mali-bad:
Documented position. The UK welcomes 2690 but would not have chosen withdrawal amid Mali/Sahel instability and humanitarian need. It pays tribute to MINUSMA personnel and condolences to those killed; it doubts Wagner delivers lasting security. All Algiers-agreement signatories should comply, and the UN should consider an entity for dialogue/implementation. The UK regrets not securing a more prudent timeline and a mandate for continued drawdown support; civilian protection is discontinued from October. 31 December is an objective; regular Secretary-General reports should inform Council revision if safety requires. Mali must cooperate, honour the SOFA until departure, uphold freedom of movement and end import restrictions. The UK continues supporting Mali, urging free/fair presidential elections in February 2024 and national civilian protection under IHRL/IHL.

Analytical application. X's fixed deadline, closed dialogue and import/movement restrictions conflict with these priorities. Arrange SOFA-protected convoys and unhindered imports, with checks parallel to movement; seek Council review informed by regular progress reports and propose the dialogue entity. Safer movement and continuity may take longer or require resources; distinguish a recommended adjustment from an actual mandate extension.

Authority. Welcoming 2690 does not endorse X, mean the UK wanted immediate withdrawal or guarantee a future vote; real support for Mali remains.

targets.sanctions-absent:
Documented position. India's national speech treats Article 41 sanctions as provisional, not an end: preserve intended impact without worsening suffering. Legitimate trade/economic activity of the targeted State and regional partners, and unintended humanitarian effects require attention and effective redress. India engaged constructively in negotiating 2664, which supports timely humanitarian/basic-needs assistance and predictable, safeguarded agency operations. India cautions against 1267-listed groups enjoying State hospitality in terrorist havens and posing as humanitarian/civil-society organizations exploiting aid cover to raise funds, recruit and evade sanctions; exemptions must neither expand terror nor politically mainstream terror entities. Due diligence remains essential. India sought a proactive 1267 Monitoring Team role and robust reporting; those concerns were not fully addressed in the adopted text. It hopes implementation review and Team feedback correct the shortcoming. This national span does not supply India's vote label.

Analytical application. New Team/reporting provisions answer that component of India's request, without rewriting 2664. Weeks of universal recipient clearance still withhold verified ready relief. Release it immediately while recipient checks/reporting proceed in parallel, and task the Team with targeted diversion tracing and follow-up. This reduces pre-delivery certainty and may leave residual diversion risk; prompt civilian relief and effective security scrutiny both matter.

Authority. No supplied national statement establishes official endorsement of X or a guaranteed future vote. Actual concerns and correction hopes remain; these recommended revisions are not official vote conditions.

targets.haiti-bad:
Documented position. Brazil speaks nationally, separately from its Council presidency. It voted for 2699's Chapter VII Mission authorization responding to urgent security needs and formal requests from Haiti, Kenya and Caribbean countries. Haiti's sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity, and international law including IHL/IHRL/UN Charter, remain fundamental. Security is crucial but coordinated institutional/socioeconomic work must address structural causes. Haitians must forge their own path through broad political consensus and free/fair/transparent elections; outside assistance alone cannot secure lasting success. Brazil is prepared to continue cooperation and consider a Mission contribution, without a troop/funding pledge. It calls for a complete arms embargo, disarming gangs/paramilitaries and citizen security/social peace; strong resumed humanitarian aid and generous sustainable economic/social assistance. Mission security should enable democratic/administrative rebuilding and economic activity.

Analytical application. X wrongly excludes political/development work, suspends rights and holds all aid until total gang defeat. Release verified urgent supplies immediately with safeguards; run Haitian-led dialogue/institutional/economic recovery alongside targeted arms enforcement and disarmament. Protecting civilians, accountability and access may slow immediate security operations; manage that cost without making gang elimination a universal aid gate.

Authority. The actual 2699 yes neither endorses every part of X nor guarantees the next vote. Real cooperation and contribution consideration remain.

targets.brazil-mali-bad:
Documented position. Brazil's national post-vote speaker De Almeida Filho hoped to renew MINUSMA on 30 June 2023, assessing its contribution positively. It acknowledges concerns of Mali's transitional authorities and host-government consent as essential to peace operations. Brazil pays tribute to peacekeepers and civilians killed while protecting UN personnel and Mali's people. It thanks Special Representative El-Ghassim Wane and reiterates support for his drawdown work. Constructive engagement should prepare task transfer and withdrawal while sustaining political transition and durable peace. Brazil supports Algeria's mediation leadership, urging all Malian political forces to remain in dialogue and redouble full peace-agreement implementation. This own-country span supplies no vote label, UK-specific Wagner claim, fixed exit date or SOFA demand.

Analytical application. X contradicts consent, safe continuity and dialogue, and misstates Brazil's renewal preference. Coordinate safe phased departure and task handover with Malian authorities; sustain Algeria-led dialogue and peace-agreement implementation throughout. Careful transfer can delay exit and require resources; manage that cost while respecting consent. These proposals do not recreate a renewed mandate.

Authority. Neither the historical speech nor compatible repairs establish official Brazil endorsement of X or guarantee a future vote. Real documented commitments, willingness and hopes remain.

targets.france-climate-bad:
Documented position. De Rivière's national 9 December 2021 debate statement supports Council attention to climate/security threats. Desertification, scarce water/resources and food insecurity can aggravate tensions and armed-group exploitation; better resource allocation can help prevention. Climate and sustainable development should reinforce each other. France highlights the Senegal-to-Djibouti Great Green Wall: $19 billion earmarked; 2030 goals of 250 million hectares restored, 10 million jobs and 250 million tonnes of carbon capture. These are collective funding/plans, not completed outcomes or a new French pledge. France seeks predictable sustainable UN logistical/financial support for the G5 Sahel Joint Force alongside development/climate action. Council prevention should use regional assessment, unity, compromise and coordination. Armed forces and peacekeepers alone cannot solve these crises. After COP26, France calls for firm lasting emissions reductions and is fully committed to that fight.

Analytical application. X overstates causation, excludes development and falsely turns plans into achievements/pledges. Combine region-specific risk assessment and resource/development measures with security support; track Great Green Wall milestones as future collective goals. Prevention and coordination require resources and can delay immediate security responses; military action alone leaves structural risks intact.

Authority. Neither the historical speech nor compatible repairs establish official France endorsement of X or guarantee a future vote. Real documented commitments, willingness and hopes remain.

targets.india-climate-bad:
Documented position. Tirumurti's national 9 December 2021 debate statement condemns Sahel/Lake Chad terrorism, including the MINUSMA attack killing seven Togolese peacekeepers and a Malian. India supports regional/G5 efforts, requiring training, logistics and predictable sustainable resources. Climate action belongs in inclusive, equitable UNFCCC/COP consensus with national commitments, rather than a disruptive separate Council platform. India recognizes climate impacts and exacerbated conflicts, but rejects climate-only causation and justification of terrorism. Following Glasgow, India announces 2030 targets: GDP emissions intensity down 45% versus 2005; 50% installed electricity capacity non-fossil; projected emissions down one billion tonnes; 500GW non-fossil capacity; net zero2070. These are targets, not achievements. ISA, UK-partnered Green Grids and CDRI/island resilience advance cooperation. Developed countries should fulfil equitable finance/technology obligations; the $1trillion call is not an Indian pledge. India remains willing to expand counterterrorism capacity-building and Council support for G5, alongside separate established climate mechanisms. No vote label is supplied.

Analytical application. X excludes participants, collapses causes, removes needed G5 support and mislabels targets. Restore inclusive UNFCCC/COP climate decisions and future-target tracking; sustain G5 training/logistics/predictable finance with equitable climate assistance. Consensus can take longer than exclusive decisions, but exclusion sacrifices participation and implementation; climate work does not replace counterterrorism.

Authority. Neither the historical speech nor compatible repairs establish official India endorsement of X or guarantee a future vote. Real documented commitments, willingness and hopes remain.
